subject: History
description: Three Sangams, Cheras-Cholas-Pandyas, Tolkappiyam, Silappadikaram, Madurai

questions.stem: The Sangam Age in South Indian history corresponds approximately to which centuries?
questions.explanation: Sangam Age — roughly 300 BCE to 300 CE — golden age of early Tamil literature. 'Sangam' (Tamil: 'assembly / academy') refers to gatherings of poets and scholars under royal patronage. Three Sangams traditionally noted in the Iraiyanar Akapporul (8th C CE commentary): First (Madurai, submerged), Second (Kapatapuram, also submerged), Third (Madurai again, the surviving works are from this). The post-Sangam age (300-600 CE) is sometimes called the 'Kalabhra Interregnum'.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The three major dynasties of the Sangam Age were:
questions.explanation: Three crowned kingdoms — 'Mu-Vendar' (the three vendars/kings). Cheras (capital Vanji/Karur, ruled today's Kerala + western TN; emblem — bow); Cholas (capital Uraiyur or Puhar/Kaveripattinam, ruled central TN + delta of Kaveri; emblem — tiger); Pandyas (capital Madurai, southern TN; emblem — fish). Pallavas, Pandavas (other) and Chalukyas came later. Sangam works also mention smaller chieftains called Velirs.

questions.stem: Tolkappiyam — the oldest extant work of Tamil grammar — was composed by:
questions.explanation: Tolkappiyam — composed by Tolkappiyar (real name disputed; possibly Trinadhumagni). Treats grammar in 3 sections — Eluttu (letters/phonology), Sol (words/morphology), Porul (subject matter / poetics). The Porul-adigaram is unique — it is essentially the world's oldest known sociolinguistic / poetics treatise. Often dated 3rd-2nd century BCE. Other Sangam authors: Ilango Adigal (Silappadikaram), Sattanar (Manimekalai), Thiruvalluvar (Tirukkural — post-Sangam, ~5th C CE).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Silappadikaram — one of the 'Five Great Epics' (Aim-perum-kappiyangal) of Tamil literature — was composed by:
questions.explanation: Silappadikaram ('Tale of the Anklet') — composed by Ilango Adigal, brother of Chera king Senguttuvan. Tells the story of Kannagi avenging the wrongful execution of her husband Kovalan in Madurai. The Five Great Epics: Silappadikaram, Manimekalai (sequel by Sattanar), Civaka Cintamani, Valayapathi, Kundalakesi. Auvaiyar — famous female Sangam poet, wrote moralistic verses (Aathichoodi). Paranar and Mamulanar — Sangam-period poets.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The capital of the Pandya dynasty during the Sangam Age, also famous for hosting the Third Sangam, was:
questions.explanation: Madurai — Pandyan capital, situated on the Vaigai river, often called 'Athens of the East'. Hosted the Third Sangam (the only one whose works survive). Famous shrine — Meenakshi Amman temple (inner sanctum dates to ~6th C; main structure 16th-17th C Nayak period). Pandyas struck punch-marked silver coins; mentioned in Megasthenes (Indica) and the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea. Karur was the Chera capital, Uraiyur the early Chola capital.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Tirukkural — the celebrated Tamil treatise on ethics and life — was composed by:
questions.explanation: Tirukkural — 1330 couplets (kurals) divided into three books: Aram (virtue/dharma), Porul (wealth/artha), Inbam (love/kama). Composed by Thiruvalluvar — usually dated to ~3rd-5th century CE (post-Sangam). Has been translated into 80+ languages. Each kural is a couplet of 7 metrical units (4+3). Its statue at Kanyakumari is 133 ft tall (1 ft per 10 kurals), unveiled by President Narayanan on 1 January 2000.

questions.stem: The two main divisions of Sangam literature based on theme are:
questions.explanation: Sangam poetry classified by theme into Akam ('inner / love') and Puram ('outer / public — war, valour, kingship, ethics'). The Akam tradition relates emotions to one of five 'tinai' (landscape archetypes): Kurinji (mountain — union of lovers), Mullai (forest — patient waiting), Marudam (cropland — quarrels), Neithal (coast — separation), Palai (desert — elopement / parting). Puram themes — Vetchi, Karandai, Vanji, Kanji, Ulinai, Tumbai, Vakai (each a stage of military expedition).
